hero.title: Your Customer Evidence Review.
hero.intro: Bring your customer-learning work into one bounded review. Decide what to keep, revise, investigate or pause, and hand off an honest next test without claiming demand is validated.

scenes.title: Gather the learning pack
scenes.narration: Bring your neutral guide, recruitment plan, conversation logs and findings review together. Check whether each source is actual, planned or rehearsal. A completed lesson is not a completed customer interview.

scenes.title: Review the question
scenes.narration: State the assumption and customer context you were exploring. Ask what these sources can establish and what they cannot. Customer accounts can inform a problem explanation; they do not automatically prove future behaviour or payment.

scenes.title: Summarise without inflation
scenes.narration: Summarise findings with anonymous source codes and source quality. Preserve conflicting accounts, missing details, selection limits and alternative explanations. If no actual research exists, mark the evidence unknown.

scenes.title: Assess the assumption
scenes.visual: Editable supported-within-scope / weakened / mixed / unknown cards
scenes.narration: Use a reasoned assessment: supported within scope, weakened, mixed or unknown. Explain the evidence and limits instead of giving a fake confidence score. Practice sources cannot support real customer claims.

scenes.title: Choose the next learning move
scenes.visual: Editable keep / revise / investigate / pause cards
scenes.narration: Keep a bounded working assumption, revise it, investigate missing evidence or pause when access and safeguards are unresolved. None of these means the venture is approved to launch. Choose the next small permitted test with a clear evidence rule.

scenes.title: Close the module honestly
scenes.narration: Create your Customer Evidence Review Brief with assessment, learning decision, next test and owner. Module completion requires all five lessons separately. It records learning progress, not verified demand or production readiness.

blocks.prompt:
Create an engaging LYNQ Academy explainer and customer-evidence checkpoint demo: Module 2.2 Lesson 30 — Your Customer Evidence Review. Editorial target 150 seconds, 16:9 1080p. Navy #0B2338, teal #087D79, mint #BCF2DF, white. Diverse adults in a contemporary Dubai workspace; warm plain English narration. Fictional review examples only, labeled Illustrative rehearsal in post. Teach source status, evidence limits, assumption assessment, keep/revise/investigate/pause decisions and a next permitted value/behaviour test. No fabricated research, quotes, counts, confidence scores, traction, demand, payment or launch-approval claims.

First provide timings, storyboard and shot prompts. Generate short shots supported by the selected Gemini/Veo account; assemble with separately recorded approved narration. Add exact branding, captions and editable Assumption / Evidence / Limits / Assessment / Decision / Next test cards in post; no generated UI/text/logos. Record approved actual Lesson 30 worksheet using explicitly fictional rehearsal data. Deliver H.264 MP4, editable project, audio, transcript, VTT/SRT, thumbnail and rights/provenance. Native-reviewed Arabic narration and RTL graphics separately. Review source honesty, privacy, pacing, audio and mobile readability. Only fictional role-play exists. Customer evidence: unknown. Decision: investigate with permitted real conversations before making customer claims. Next value/behaviour test remains a plan, with access pending. No demand or payment is established.

A problem conversation does not automatically demonstrate adoption or willingness to pay. If you proceed to value/behaviour testing, specify the claim, observable evidence, review rule and stop conditions before execution. Do not reuse a compliment as purchase proof.
